headword: {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}

definitions.explanation: A company whose ownership and/or management is concentrated in the hands of a single family or a small number of related families. The term covers everything from small neighborhood shops to large publicly listed corporations in which the founding family retains a controlling stake or holds key executive posts.

notes:
Composed of {同族|どうぞく} (same family; same clan) and ⟦{企業|きぎょう}→企業：00225_kigyou⟧ (enterprise; company). The {族|ぞく} here refers to the family lineage rather than ethnicity.

USAGE:
A neutral, descriptive term used in business news, accounting and tax contexts, and corporate governance discussions. Note the specialized tax-law sense: under Japan's Corporation Tax Act, a {同族会社|どうぞくがいしゃ} is a company in which three or fewer shareholders together own more than 50% of the shares — a status that triggers special anti-tax-avoidance rules. Outside of tax law, the everyday meaning is broader and synonymous with 'family business.' The reading ⟦どう→どう：00543_dou⟧ぞく is fixed; do not confuse with {同属|どうぞく} 'of the same genus.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経営|けいえい}→経営：02740_keiei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to run a family business
- {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{継|つ}ぐ→継ぐ：02292_tsugu⟧: to inherit/take over a family business
- ⟦{大手|おおて}→大手：12171_oote⟧{同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}: a major family-owned company
- {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後継者|こうけいしゃ}→後継者：12592_koukeisha⟧: successor in a family business

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {同族会社|どうぞくがいしゃ}: family company — narrower technical term used in tax law
- {家族経営|かぞくけいえい}: family management — emphasizes management by family members; often a smaller scale
- ⟦{老舗|しにせ}→老舗：16152_shinise⟧: long-established business — emphasizes age and tradition; many ⟦{老舗|しにせ}→老舗：16152_shinise⟧ are also {同族企業|どうぞくきぎょう}
